Each scenario: reference arm runs TWICE (determinism control), then the facade arm; the facade 'state' digest must equal the reference 'state' digest bitwise (IEEE-754 bit patterns via struct.pack for floats, WKB sha256 for geometries incl. component-level collection digests, dtypes/columns/orderings, exact strings). Presentation randomness excluded from digests by design: the time-based progress prints are reduced to their deterministic line counts; raw timings and traceback text (arm-dependent file paths) are never recorded. Error messages are recorded verbatim except one documented normalization: validate_zonal_ready's TypeError interpolates each arm's own Zonal class qualname (the annotation-alias delta established in the paths reflection), normalized by replacing the exact repr token.

new_pinned_upstream_facts.node_builder_lexsort_truncation: NEW DEFECT, bounded reproduction retained (scenario node_builder_truncation). vectorized_node_edge_builder (upstream madina/zonal/network_utils.py, def at :80; np.lexsort at :96; node_first_occurance built at :111) assigns edge endpoint labels by walking unique-point occurrence ranges derived from node_first_occurance (loop at :128); the final range is '[last_first_occurrence, last_first_occurrence + 1)' — the lexicographic maximum point's REMAINING occurrences are never processed and their edge labels keep the zeros initialization. The dead statement 'np.append(node_first_occurance, point_count - 1)' at :123 (result discarded — np.append is not in-place) is the vestigial intended fix; function returns at :140. [Line citations corrected per review finding M2.] Observed on a 7-edge grid: C=(100,100) is the lexsort maximum with three occurrences; edge 2 (B-C) gets end=0 (F, a phantom 50 m attachment instead of C at the true 50 m), and the A-C diagonal is mislabeled {1,0} — the same endpoint set as edge 0 (F-A) — so _discard_redundant_edges DELETES a genuinely distinct street. Consequence chain: origin o3 (mid B-C) attaches to F instead of C and its accessibility scope is EMPTY (pinned), while the node table's degree counts (from np.unique) look normal — the corruption is silent at the network-construction surface. The facade reproduces all of it bitwise (faithful copy, bugs included). Clean-fixture contrast: a lexicographic maximum occurring exactly once is unaffected — the ACCESS fixture set is designed around this (the clean grid adds a C-G stub whose far corner is the unique maximum). BUG-REGISTRY CANDIDATE: handoff recorded in receipt (bug_registry.json is outside this task's owned files); also a corrected_v1 fix candidate for SCIENCE review.
